transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Kim (HighTower, Head of AI), Miguel Torres (HighTower, CTO), Nina Shah (HighTower, PM)
Links shared: Redwood_POC_Deck.pdf (link), /redwood/docs/golden-prompts.xlsx (link), initial-benchmark-template.csv (link)

00:00 Maya: OK everyone hi thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros. I'm Maya, AE on this account, I run the POC for Redwood inference.
00:12 Dr. Kim: Hi Maya, Laura here. Excited to dig in.
00:15 Miguel: Miguel Torres, CTO. We have a pretty strict timeline so want to get scope nailed.
00:19 Nina: Nina, product. I'll own the sample set and evaluation rubric on our side.
00:25 Daniel: Daniel Chen, SE, I'll lead the benchmarks and setup. Couple of notes upfront: we'll propose hosted + dedicated baseline then discuss Private if you need VPC.

02:05 Maya: Objective for today is to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, and then agree on the quality eval plan - golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, formatting checks, and a scoring approach.

04:00 Dr. Kim: Quick context - we want to replace some of our rules-based triage and clinician note summarization. Target latency for interactive triage is sub 700ms 95p; cost target is roughly $0.002 per convo token equivalent - like we're sensitive to both.

05:10 Daniel: OK latency vs cost tradeoff is classic - we'll run the same workload against an optimized open model on Redwood Hosted and a Dedicated pool with quantized weights. We'll capture p95, p99, and tokens/sec. Also will capture cost per 1k tokens from our billing sim.

06:30 Miguel: For data residency we may need Private later, but initial POC can be hosted if data is pseudo-anonymized. Need to confirm audit logs, KMS support.

07:12 Maya: Noted. For SOC2 and KMS, we'll send the security pack. Private POC checklist will show what we need for network access.

09:00 Nina: On quality - we want golden prompts for the two main flows: triage routing and note summarization. Each flow should have golden outputs so we can run automated regression. How many golds do we need?

10:20 Daniel: Good q. For an initial quality pass have at least 200-300 golden prompts per flow to catch obvious regressions. For a more robust eval do 1k per flow. For production acceptance we recommend 5k combined across flows with stratified edge cases.

12:40 Dr. Kim: That seems reasonable. For hallucination detection we need both factuality checks and domain-specific safety checks - e.g., suggest treatments not allowed. How will we test hallucinations?

14:05 Daniel: We'll do automated hallucination checks using reference data where applicable - for example, in summarization we can compare extracted medication mentions against the EHR ground truth. For free-text assertions we'll apply a classifier and manual spot-checking. Regression tests will include hallucination flags and a threshold of tolerance.

16:10 Maya: Could you outline the scoring approach? Nina wants to know how you'll convert model outputs into a pass/fail or score we can use for A/B.

17:00 Daniel: Absolutely. Proposed scoring: a weighted composite metric - correctness (40%), format adherence (20%), hallucination score (20%), latency/throughput penalty (20%). Each subcomponent is normalized 0-100, we compute weighted average. For pass threshold we'll discuss but propose >= 80 for move-to-prod.

19:30 Nina: Format adherence - what's in scope? We need structured JSON with specific fields, including codes. If the model deviates we fail the example. Are you going to auto-validate schema?

20:20 Daniel: Yes schema validation is automated in the eval harness. We'll compare to your JSON schema; any missing required fields or type mismatch is a hard fail for that sample, but overall score accounts for partials so you can see per-field pass rates.

22:10 Miguel: On benchmarks - workload sizing. Our production is ~120k requests/day, 95% are triage short prompts (averaging 40 tokens) and 5% long summarizations (avg 700 tokens). For POC what's the right sample size?

23:30 Daniel: For performance benchmarking we'll run synthetic load that mirrors that mix. Initial run 1k prompts (fast path), then a 10k stress run. Quality evals operate on the 5k combined golden set. The 1k baseline gives quick signals and cost numbers; 10k stress shows autoscaling behavior.

25:00 Maya: Timeline check: we want results before leadership sync on 2026-04-15. That gives about two weeks. Is that feasible?

26:12 Daniel: Timeline proposed: 1) By 2026-04-02 Redwood sends golden prompts template and security docs. 2) By 2026-04-06 Redwood completes 1k baseline benchmark with hosted + dedicated variants and shares results. 3) By 2026-04-09 runbook + security follow-up. 4) By 2026-04-13 finish 5k quality eval and deliver the report so you can present on 4/15. Feasible if sample set is provided on 4/05 latest.

28:00 Dr. Kim: Sounds tight but doable. One blocker is access to de-identified clinical notes; Nina will provide. Also we need to evaluate hallucination risk scoring more conservatively - given clinical setting, set pass threshold maybe 85 not 80.

29:10 Nina: Agreed - let's set pass threshold to 85 for safety-critical flows (note summarization) and we can be 80 for triage.

30:00 Daniel: We'll surface per-flow thresholds in the report. Also we'll include failure modes: hallucination examples, missing schema fields, and worst-case latency spikes.

31:45 Maya: Security asks - Miguel, you mentioned network requirements for Private. Can you list what you need for the Private sandbox?

32:10 Miguel: We'll need IP allowlist, SAML SSO integration, and KMS with customer-managed keys - plus audit logs retained 1 year. Also encryption at rest.

33:20 Daniel: Redwood Private supports SAML and customer KMS; audit logs are available with the enterprise package. I'll flag the exact artifacts in the security pack.

34:50 Dr. Kim: A few specific quality items: 1) golden prompts for edge cases (misspellings, shorthand from clinicians), 2) hallucination taxonomy (clinical hallucination, hallucinated meds, hallucinated dates), 3) format strictness for JSON and codes.

36:15 Daniel: We'll add those categories to the eval harness. For hallucination taxonomy we'll produce labels and automatic heuristics plus a manual review sample (5-10%). We'll export per-sample evidence to a spreadsheet so triage on failures is easy.

38:00 Nina: On regression testing cadence - after POC, how often should we run the regression suite? Nightly? Weekly?

39:10 Daniel: For POC and initial rollout we suggest daily runs of the regression suite (smoke + sampling) and weekly full runs against the 5k golden set. The CI can fail builds if hallucination rate increases beyond a threshold.

40:45 Maya: Pricing note - we'll send a simple estimate for hosted vs dedicated cost for the expected daily volume. Dedicated will lower per-token costs but adds committed spend. We'll include the Optimize recommendations (batching/quantization) in the estimate.

42:05 Miguel: If the model needs to be quantized or use KV cache optimizations, what's the impact on quality?

43:00 Daniel: Quantization (int8/4-bit) can slightly change outputs - our eval harness will compare BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics and the weighted score; we'll flag regressions. For risky flows we recommend keeping a higher-precision variant as fallback. Redwood's smart routing can fallback automatically.

44:20 Dr. Kim: Good. For the report, please include a short appendix with sample prompts that failed and why. That helps our clinical reviewers.

45:00 Maya: Yep we'll include failure examples, per-field error rates, hallucination taxonomy, and remediation suggestions.

46:10 Daniel: Last check - access to the sandbox. Miguel, can you confirm the firewall window and the person who will approve IPs?

46:30 Miguel: I'll get with infra team and confirm by 2026-04-04. Approver will be me.

47:10 Maya: Great - recap of next steps: we'll send the golden prompts template and security docs 4/2, you provide 5k sample by 4/5, we'll do 1k benchmark by 4/6 and 5k quality pass by 4/13, follow-up runbook + security meeting 4/9. Action items noted. Thanks everyone.

47:45 Dr. Kim: Thanks all.

47:50 End of recording.
